# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 10
**Agent:** LOGOS (Formal Equivalence)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 10

---

*[An interlude: vision of the righteous martyrs. Then the punishing angel Tartaruchus. Return to the damned.]*

1. Another angel came running to meet us, joyful and radiant, and said: "Come — I will show you the righteous who were persecuted and killed for righteousness' sake."

2. He led us to a pleasant place, a place full of every delight, shining with the light of the sun.

3. When we had entered that place, I, Peter, saw all the righteous who had been persecuted and killed for righteousness' sake.

4. Their faces shone like the sun, and they were clothed in fine white linen; their mouths were open and they praised the Lord God their God.

5. I saw the men — those who had suffered for my name's sake. Their beauty was radiant, more beautiful than anything I had seen in all the world.

6. Their appearance was bright, their beauty great, and their light was as the light of the sun.

7. The angel Tartaruchus, who is set over the punishments, said to me: "Look also upon those who were put to shame in the world and subjected to the power of men."

8. In an outer place I saw an angel of fierce aspect who had oversight of the punishments. He was dressed like a man of dark complexion, and his face shone like fire.

9. He said to me: "You have seen those who receive rewards; now I will show you the punishments as well."

10. In that place I saw men and women set apart, in great torment, gnashing their teeth and weeping.

11. I asked: "Who are these?"

12. The angel said: "These are those who on earth devoted themselves to riches, neglected the poor and hungry, and did not help widows and orphans — but despised the servants of God.

13. For this reason they will be punished forever, according to the will of God."

---
*LOGOS note: "Tartaruchus" (v.7) — the name is attested only here in Christian apocalyptic. It derives from Greek Tartaros (the deepest underworld) plus *-uchos* (holder/keeper). A remarkable survival of Greek cosmological language in the Ethiopic.*
